rationale: Typed ODE contract inherited verbatim (single state h, its RHS, IC h=0.01) — only time range, fixed parameters, noise, and expectations were chosen. Physical water-like viscous film: rho=1000, g=9.81, mu=1 Pa·s, gamma=0.072, R_gas=8.314, T_temp=298, Gamma=3e-6 mol/m^2, b_slip=1e-4 m (large but attainable on superhydrophobic walls), h_evap=1e-6 m (within the suggested 1e-8..1e-6 nanometric crossover). L_drain=0.01 m was chosen to raise the 1/L^3 surface-tension and surfactant terms into clear visibility relative to the 1/L gravity term while keeping net drainage. Substitution at h=0.01,t=0 gives finite real dh_dt=-1.888. The new tanh term modulates the gravity term; since h>>h_evap the tanh saturates at 1, so the new term acts as a second gravity contribution and its child-vs-parent trajectory separation is intrinsically bounded (~1.4e-3 in h) independent of rate constants and t-range. The lever is therefore the noise yardstick: sigma=0.00025 puts the new mechanism at 5.6*sigma (passes). All terms are visible (>=30x sigma) EXCEPT the van der Waals disjoining term, which is ~15 orders too small at macroscopic thickness and cannot be excited without unphysical A_ham; it is retained as negligible. excitation_ok=true since the new mechanism (the point of this evolution step) is clearly visible.

scenario_text: A thin liquid film coats a vertical plate and drains downward under gravity, resisted by internal viscosity. The film thickness at a fixed height decreases as fluid flows away faster than it is replenished. We follow the local film thickness as it thins over time.
